objects.definition: typedef unsigned char uint8_t;
objects.description: 8-bit unsigned integer type defined here for older MSVC (pre-2013) when <inttypes.h> is unavailable.

objects.definition: typedef signed char int8_t;
objects.description: 8-bit signed integer type defined here for older MSVC (pre-2013).

objects.definition: typedef unsigned short uint16_t;
objects.description: 16-bit unsigned integer type defined here for older MSVC (pre-2013).

objects.definition: typedef signed short int16_t;
objects.description: 16-bit signed integer type defined here for older MSVC (pre-2013).

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int uint32_t;
objects.description: 32-bit unsigned integer type defined here for older MSVC (pre-2013).

objects.definition: typedef signed int int32_t;
objects.description: 32-bit signed integer type defined here for older MSVC (pre-2013).
64-bit unsigned integer type defined conditionally for older MSVC (pre-2013): uses unsigned _int64 with MSVC extensions, otherwise unsigned long long.
64-bit signed integer type defined conditionally for older MSVC (pre-2013): uses _int64 with MSVC extensions, otherwise long long.

objects.definition: typedef long suseconds_t;
objects.description: POSIX-style signed integral type for microsecond fields (e.g., timeval.tv_usec). Defined here only on Windows to provide compatibility with code expecting suseconds_t.

Macro-defined platform-abstracted socket handle type: SOCKET on Windows, int on UNIX-like systems. Note: this is a macro, not a typedef; included here for developer awareness, but there is no true C/C++ type definition in this header.

objects.definition: typedef	int bpf_int32;
objects.description: 32-bit signed integer type used by the BPF userland API for alignment and instruction fields.

objects.definition: typedef	u_int bpf_u_int32;
objects.description: 32-bit unsigned integer type used by the BPF userland API for instruction fields and constants.

Holds a compiled BPF program: bf_len is the instruction count, bf_insns points to an array of struct bpf_insn. Lifetime/ownership of bf_insns is managed by the caller or libpcap functions that create it.
Single BPF instruction. code encodes class/op/mode; jt and jf are jump offsets for conditional branches; k is an immediate/offset/length operand depending on code.

This header defines a large set of preprocessor constants (DLT_*) representing link-layer header type codes for libpcap/tcpdump. It does not declare or define any structs, enums, typedefs, or classes. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

Libpcap-specific header prepended to each Bluetooth HCI H4 frame. Contains a 32-bit field in network byte order whose least-significant bit indicates packet direction (1 = incoming). Other bits are currently unspecified. Used to annotate captured H4 frames.

Libpcap-specific header prepended to each Bluetooth Linux monitor frame. Both fields are in network byte order. adapter_id identifies the Bluetooth adapter; opcode is a monitor event opcode or frame subtype. Exact value ranges depend on the Linux Bluetooth monitor subsystem.

Header structure for SocketCAN CAN and CAN FD frames (per Linux Documentation/networking/can.rst). Contains the 29/11-bit identifier in can_id plus payload length and FD-specific flags. The reserved bytes pad/align the header for potential future use. Used to precede raw CAN or CAN FD payloads captured by libpcap on SocketCAN interfaces.

Header structure for SocketCAN CAN XL frames (per Linux can.h). The flags field (with CANXL_XLF set) distinguishes CAN XL from classic/CAN FD. Includes priority/VCID, SDU type, payload length, and an acceptance field used by CAN XL. Used to precede CAN XL payloads in captures.

Represents an Ethernet address book entry as returned by pcap_next_etherent(). Contains a 6-byte hardware (MAC) address and a fixed-size buffer for the associated host name. Used by libpcap name-to-address helper routines on systems without native /etc/ethers handling.
NFLOG base header preceding TLV records. Fields are stored in big-endian order on the wire; callers must byte-swap as needed. Contains address family, header version, and resource ID.
Generic TLV header used by NFLOG records. Length and type are in host byte order; the value immediately follows and may be big-endian or byte arrays depending on type.
TLV payload describing basic packet metadata: link-layer protocol (EtherType) and netfilter hook number. The fields appear within an NFULA_PACKET_HDR TLV.
TLV payload carrying a link-layer (hardware) address of up to 8 bytes, with recorded length. Used in NFULA_HWADDR.
TLV payload giving the skbuff timestamp: seconds and microseconds components. Used in NFULA_TIMESTAMP. Endianness on the wire is big-endian per NFLOG rules.

DLT_LINUX_SLL fake link-layer header used by libpcap for captures on Linux cooked sockets. Provides packet type, hardware address type/length, source link-layer address, and protocol, all in network byte order except the address bytes. Layout must not be changed for compatibility.

DLT_LINUX_SLL2 fake link-layer header, a successor to sll_header, adding fields for interface index and reserved bytes, and splitting sizes to single-byte pkttype and halen. Used by libpcap for newer Linux cooked captures. Fields are in network byte order except the address bytes; the reserved field must be zero.
USB control transfer setup packet header, as defined by the USB spec. Used at the start of control (S-type) packets in DLT_USB and in linux USB headers herein.
Summary information for isochronous URB transfers: error_count and number of descriptors present.
Per-event header used by Linux USB monitor (DLT_USB_LINUX). Contains event identity, transfer and endpoint info, timing, status, lengths, and an embedded control setup header when present.

Per-event header for Linux USB monitor mmap capture (DLT_USB_LINUX_MMAPPED). Extends basic header with union for control setup or isochronous summary, plus interval, start frame, transfer flags, and descriptor count.
Per-isochronous-packet descriptor that may prefix packet data for isochronous transfers; gives status, data offset, and length.

Represents an IEEE 802.1Q VLAN header/tag inserted into Ethernet frames. vlan_tpid is the Tag Protocol Identifier (typically 0x8100 for 802.1Q), and vlan_tci is the 16-bit Tag Control Information containing the PCP, DEI, and VLAN ID fields.

objects.definition: typedef	int bpf_int32;
objects.description: Alias for a 32-bit signed integer used by BPF/libpcap when older bpf.h lacks 64-bit typedefs. Used in pcap headers and file formats.

objects.definition: typedef	u_int bpf_u_int32;
objects.description: Alias for a 32-bit unsigned integer used by BPF/libpcap when older bpf.h lacks 64-bit typedefs.

objects.definition: typedef struct pcap pcap_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an active or configured pcap capture context. Actual struct is defined privately in libpcap; users manipulate it via the pcap_* API.

objects.definition: typedef struct pcap_dumper pcap_dumper_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a pcap dump file writer used with pcap_dump_* APIs.

objects.definition: typedef struct pcap_if pcap_if_t;
objects.description: Opaque alias for the pcap_if struct representing an interface in a linked list from pcap_findalldevs.

objects.definition: typedef struct pcap_addr pcap_addr_t;
objects.description: Opaque alias for the pcap_addr struct representing an interface address entry within pcap_if.
Header structure at the beginning of classic pcap savefiles. Defines file magic, version, timezone, sigfigs, snapshot length, and link-layer type.
Enumeration used with pcap_setdirection() to select capture direction: inbound+outbound, inbound only, or outbound only.
Per-packet metadata provided by libpcap: timestamp, captured length, and original packet length.
Capture statistics returned by pcap_stats(); fields vary slightly on Windows.
Linked-list node describing a capture interface: name, description, address list, and flags. Obtained from pcap_findalldevs().
Linked-list node representing an address attached to an interface, including netmask, broadcast, and destination (P2P) addresses.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*pcap_handler)(u_char *, const struct pcap_pkthdr *,
			     const u_char *);
objects.description: Callback function type used by pcap_loop()/pcap_dispatch() to deliver packets: user cookie, packet header, and packet data.
Windows-only queue of raw packets for bulk transmission using pcap_sendqueue_transmit().
Authentication parameters for RPCAP remote capture: method (NULL or username/password) and optional credentials.
Sampling configuration for Windows local captures: method (none, 1-every-N, first-after-N-ms) and associated value.
Enumeration of option identifiers used with pcap_options APIs to get/set capture options.

objects.definition: typedef struct pcap_options pcap_options;
objects.description: Opaque options container used with pcap_alloc_option()/pcap_set_option_*()/pcap_get_option_*() to configure capture/open options.
No custom types are defined in this header. It only includes <pcap/pcap.h> for backward compatibility. Types such as pcap_t are defined in the included header, not here.

functions.name: bpf_filter
functions.signature: u_int bpf_filter(const struct bpf_insn *program, const u_char *packet, u_int wirelen, u_int buflen);
functions.description: Executes a classic BPF program over a packet buffer and returns the filter result (typically the number of bytes to accept; 0 means reject). Deprecated in favor of pcap_offline_filter(). Use to run a compiled BPF instruction array against a given packet (wirelen is the original packet length, buflen is the available bytes in the passed buffer).
requirements: program must point to a valid array of struct bpf_insn representing a complete BPF program (ideally validated via bpf_validate() before use).
packet must be a valid pointer to at least buflen bytes when buflen > 0; it may be NULL only if buflen == 0.
wirelen must be the actual on-the-wire packet length (>= 0).
buflen must be the number of bytes available in packet (>= 0).
wirelen can be >=, ==, or > buflen; do not pass a buflen larger than the actual allocated buffer.
Caller must interpret the return value: 0 indicates reject, non-zero typically indicates the number of bytes to accept/copy.

functions.name: bpf_validate
functions.signature: int bpf_validate(const struct bpf_insn *f, int len);
functions.description: Validates a BPF instruction array for safety and correctness. Returns non-zero if the program is valid and safe to execute, 0 otherwise. Use before executing a program with bpf_filter() or installing it in a kernel/userland interpreter.
requirements: f must point to an array of at least len elements of struct bpf_insn.
len must be >= 0; it is the number of instructions in the program.
Caller must check the return value and avoid executing the program if validation fails (return == 0).

functions.name: bpf_image
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation (disassembly) of a single BPF instruction. Useful for debugging or printing BPF programs. The option parameter controls formatting details; specific meanings are not documented in this header (unknown). The returned string storage characteristics (e.g., static buffer vs. caller-allocated) are not specified here (unknown).
requirements: insn must be a non-null pointer to a valid struct bpf_insn to be rendered.
option is a formatting/verbosity selector; exact accepted values are unknown in this header and may be implementation-defined.
Caller should treat the returned char* as read-only; lifetime/ownership are unspecified here (may be a static buffer).

functions.name: bpf_dump
functions.signature: void bpf_dump(const struct bpf_program *program, int option);
functions.description: Prints a human-readable disassembly of a BPF program (sequence of instructions). Intended for diagnostics and debugging. The option parameter controls output formatting/verbosity; exact semantics are not documented here (unknown). Output destination is not specified in this header (commonly standard output or error; unknown).
requirements: program must be non-null and program->bf_insns must point to at least program->bf_len valid instructions.
option controls formatting/verbosity; exact accepted values are unknown in this header and may be implementation-defined.

functions.name: pcap_next_etherent
functions.description: Reads and returns the next entry from an ethers database (e.g., /etc/ethers) associated with the supplied FILE stream. Returns a pointer to a struct pcap_etherent containing the 6-byte Ethernet address and associated host name. Typical usage is to open PCAP_ETHERS_FILE and iterate until NULL is returned. Storage is likely static/non-reentrant.
requirements: The FILE* must be a valid, open stream positioned at the start of an ethers entry (commonly from PCAP_ETHERS_FILE).
The FILE* must be opened for reading; binary/text mode is platform-dependent but typical text mode is expected.
The returned struct may be backed by static storage; callers should not free it and must copy data if they need it after subsequent calls or across threads.
Not thread-safe or reentrant (implied by typical libc/ethers semantics; exact thread safety is unknown).
On end-of-file or parse error, the function may return NULL; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: pcap_ether_hostton
functions.description: Resolves a host name to its Ethernet (MAC) address, typically using an ethers database such as /etc/ethers. Returns a pointer to a 6-byte MAC address on success or NULL on failure. Intended for environments lacking native ethers support.
requirements: Input string must be a valid, null-terminated host name present in the ethers database.
The returned pointer refers to a 6-byte address; callers must not free it and should copy it before the next call if persistence is needed (likely static storage; not reentrant).
Callers must check for a NULL return to detect lookup failure.
Thread safety is unknown; assume non-reentrant behavior.

functions.name: pcap_ether_aton
functions.description: Parses a textual Ethernet address (e.g., “aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff”) and returns a pointer to a 6-byte binary MAC address. Useful for converting human-readable MAC strings to binary form.
requirements: Input must be a null-terminated MAC address string in a supported format (exact accepted formats are unknown; colon-separated hex pairs are typical).
On success, returns a pointer to 6 bytes representing the address; do not free it and copy if persistence is required (likely static storage; not reentrant).
Callers must check for NULL return to detect parse/format errors.
Thread safety is unknown; assume non-reentrant behavior.

functions.name: pcap_nametoaddr
functions.description: Deprecated (not reentrant). Resolves a host name to one or more IPv4 addresses and returns a non-reentrant array of pointers to bpf_u_int32 addresses, likely in network byte order, terminated in an implementation-defined way. Use pcap_nametoaddrinfo instead.
requirements: Input must be a null-terminated host name.
Function is explicitly deprecated and not reentrant; do not use in multithreaded contexts and prefer pcap_nametoaddrinfo.
Returned storage ownership and lifetime are unspecified; assume static storage—do not free and copy values if needed beyond the next call.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect lookup failure.
Address byte order and array termination details are unknown; callers must not assume formatting beyond being IPv4-sized values.

functions.name: pcap_nametoaddrinfo
functions.description: Resolves a host name to one or more addresses and returns a linked list of addrinfo results (similar to getaddrinfo). This is the reentrant replacement for pcap_nametoaddr. Caller is responsible for freeing the list.
requirements: Input must be a null-terminated host name.
On success, returns a non-NULL struct addrinfo*; on failure returns NULL—caller must check for NULL.
Caller must free the returned list with freeaddrinfo when done.
Address families, flags, and canonical name behavior are unspecified; caller should examine the returned addrinfo fields.

functions.name: pcap_nametonetaddr
functions.description: Resolves a network name to an IPv4 network address (e.g., for a named network). Returns a 32-bit value representing the network address; failure-indication semantics are not specified in this header.
requirements: Input must be a null-terminated network name.
Caller must interpret the return value carefully; whether 0 signifies failure or a valid address is unknown from this header.
Returned address byte order (host vs. network) is not specified; callers should treat it as implementation-defined.

functions.name: pcap_nametoport
functions.signature: PCAP_API int pcap_nametoport(const char *, int *, int *);
functions.description: Parses or resolves a service/port specification to a numeric port and associated protocol (e.g., tcp/udp). It returns the protocol along with the port number via output parameters; if the protocol is unknown or ambiguous, PROTO_UNDEF (-1) is used. Exact return value semantics (success/failure code vs. protocol) are not specified here.
requirements: First argument must be a null-terminated service/port string (e.g., a service name from /etc/services or a numeric port; exact formats unknown).
Second argument (int*) must be non-NULL and will receive the port number on success.
Third argument (int*) must be non-NULL and will receive the protocol indicator; PROTO_UNDEF (-1) indicates unknown/ambiguous protocol.
Caller must check the function's return value and/or output parameters to detect failure; exact conventions are unknown from this header.

functions.name: pcap_nametoportrange
functions.signature: PCAP_API int pcap_nametoportrange(const char *, int *, int *, int *);
functions.description: Parses a port range or service-range specification and provides the low and high port bounds and associated protocol (e.g., tcp/udp). Returns information via output parameters; if the protocol is unknown or ambiguous, PROTO_UNDEF (-1) is used. Exact return value semantics are not specified here.
requirements: First argument must be a null-terminated string representing a port range or service range (formats such as "start-end" are likely, but exact grammar is unspecified).
Second argument (int*) must be non-NULL and will receive the low port on success.
Third argument (int*) must be non-NULL and will receive the high port on success.
Fourth argument (int*) must be non-NULL and will receive the protocol indicator; PROTO_UNDEF (-1) indicates unknown/ambiguous protocol.
Caller must check the function's return value and/or outputs to detect failure; exact conventions are unknown from this header.

functions.name: pcap_nametoproto
functions.description: Resolves an IP protocol name (e.g., "tcp", "udp", "icmp") to its numeric protocol value. Returns PROTO_UNDEF (-1) if the protocol is unknown.
requirements: Input must be a null-terminated protocol name string.
Caller must check for PROTO_UNDEF (-1) to detect unknown names.

functions.name: pcap_nametoeproto
functions.description: Resolves an Ethernet protocol name (e.g., an ethertype like "ip", "arp") to its numeric Ethernet protocol value. Returns PROTO_UNDEF (-1) if the protocol is unknown.
requirements: Input must be a null-terminated Ethernet protocol name string.
Caller must check for PROTO_UNDEF (-1) to detect unknown names.

functions.name: pcap_nametollc
functions.description: Resolves an LLC protocol name to its numeric LLC value. Returns PROTO_UNDEF (-1) if the protocol is unknown.
requirements: Input must be a null-terminated LLC protocol name string.
Caller must check for PROTO_UNDEF (-1) to detect unknown names.

functions.name: pcap_init
functions.description: Initializes libpcap with library-wide options before any capture handles are created. Typical callers pass 0 for default behavior or PCAP_CHAR_ENC_* and PCAP_MMAP_32BIT flags as needed. On error, returns a negative PCAP_ERROR code and sets errbuf.
requirements: errbuf must be a non-null buffer of at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
May be called once early in program startup; if not called, libpcap defaults to legacy-compatible behavior.
Callers must check the return value (PCAP_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).
opts is a bitmask of PCAP_CHAR_ENC_LOCAL, PCAP_CHAR_ENC_UTF_8, and PCAP_MMAP_32BIT; other bits are reserved.

functions.name: pcap_lookupdev
functions.description: Deprecated helper that returns the name of the first suitable capture device on the local host. Prefer pcap_findalldevs().
requirements: errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Function is deprecated; behavior can be non-thread-safe or platform-specific.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errbuf for details.

functions.name: pcap_lookupnet
functions.signature: int pcap_lookupnet(const char *device, bpf_u_int32 *netp, bpf_u_int32 *maskp, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Retrieves the IPv4 network number and netmask for the given interface name.
requirements: device may be NULL for default behavior on some platforms; typically pass an interface name from pcap_findalldevs().
netp and maskp must be valid non-null pointers to receive results.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; caller must check return (PCAP_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).

functions.name: pcap_create
functions.description: Creates an inactive capture handle for the named device. Use setter functions (snaplen, promisc, timeout, etc.) and then pcap_activate() to start capturing.
requirements: device should name a capture device; for files use pcap_open_offline().
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and use errbuf.
After creation, call configuration setters before pcap_activate().

functions.name: pcap_set_snaplen
functions.description: Sets the snapshot length (maximum captured bytes per packet) on an inactive pcap handle.
requirements: p must be a valid pcap_t* returned by pcap_create() and not yet activated.
snaplen should be a non-negative integer; 0 implies a platform default.
Returns 0 on success, PCAP_ERROR_* on failure; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_promisc
functions.description: Enables or disables promiscuous mode on an inactive capture handle.
requirements: p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
promisc is non-zero to enable, zero to disable.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_can_set_rfmon
functions.description: Queries whether the device could support monitor (rfmon) mode.
requirements: p must be a valid (usually inactive) pcap handle for a device.
Returns 0/1 or PCAP_ERROR_* codes; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_rfmon
functions.description: Requests monitor (rfmon) mode for an inactive capture handle if supported by the device.
requirements: p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
rfmon non-zero enables request; zero disables.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.
Use pcap_can_set_rfmon() to check support beforehand.

functions.name: pcap_set_timeout
functions.description: Sets the read timeout, in milliseconds, on an inactive capture handle.
requirements: p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
to_ms should be >= 0; semantics may vary by platform.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_tstamp_type
functions.description: Requests a specific timestamp type for an inactive capture handle (e.g., host vs adapter timestamps).
requirements: p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
tstamp_type should be one of PCAP_TSTAMP_* values supported by the device.
Returns 0 on success, PCAP_ERROR_CANTSET_TSTAMP_TYPE or other PCAP_ERROR_* on failure; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_immediate_mode
functions.description: Enables or disables immediate mode, delivering packets to user space as soon as they arrive rather than buffering.
requirements: p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
immediate non-zero enables; zero disables.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_buffer_size
functions.description: Sets the kernel or capture buffer size (bytes) for an inactive handle, if supported by the platform/driver.
requirements: p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
buffer_size should be a positive integer.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_tstamp_precision
functions.description: Requests timestamp resolution (microsecond or nanosecond) for an inactive capture handle.
requirements: p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
tstamp_precision must be PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_MICRO or PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_NANO, and must be supported by the device/platform.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_TSTAMP_PRECISION_NOTSUP/other errors; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_get_tstamp_precision
functions.description: Gets the active timestamp precision of a handle (after activation or when reading from a savefile).
requirements: p must be a valid pcap handle (active or offline).
Returns PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_* or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_activate
functions.description: Activates an inactive capture handle previously created with pcap_create(), applying all configured options and opening the capture device.
requirements: p must be created by pcap_create() and not yet activated or closed.
After activation, option setters (set_snaplen, set_promisc, etc.) can no longer be called on this handle.
Returns 0 or a positive PCAP_WARNING_* on success, or a negative PCAP_ERROR_* on failure; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_list_tstamp_types
functions.description: Retrieves the list of timestamp types supported by the device for the given handle.
requirements: p must be a valid handle (typically inactive before activation).
tstamp_types must be a valid non-null pointer to receive an allocated array; free it with pcap_free_tstamp_types().
Returns a non-negative count on success or PCAP_ERROR_* on failure; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_free_tstamp_types
functions.description: Frees an array returned by pcap_list_tstamp_types().
requirements: tstamp_types must be a pointer previously returned by pcap_list_tstamp_types(), or NULL.
Do not use tstamp_types after freeing.

functions.name: pcap_tstamp_type_name_to_val
functions.description: Converts a timestamp type name string to its integer constant value.
requirements: name must be a valid null-terminated string.
Returns a non-negative type value or PCAP_ERROR_* if unknown; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_tstamp_type_val_to_name
functions.description: Returns the canonical name string for a timestamp type value, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: tstamp_type should be a PCAP_TSTAMP_* value.
Caller must check for NULL result before use.

functions.name: pcap_tstamp_type_val_to_description
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description for a timestamp type value, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: tstamp_type should be a PCAP_TSTAMP_* value.
Caller must check for NULL result before use.

functions.name: pcap_set_protocol_linux
functions.description: Linux-only: sets the capture protocol on packet sockets (e.g., ETH_P_*).
requirements: Available only when compiled on Linux (__linux__).
p must be from pcap_create() and not yet activated.
protocol must be a valid Linux ETH_P_* value or similar; semantics are OS-specific.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_open_live
functions.signature: pcap_t *pcap_open_live(const char *device, int snaplen, int promisc, int to_ms, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Opens and activates a live capture handle for the given device in one step, configuring snapshot length, promiscuous mode, and read timeout.
requirements: device is the name of a capture device (NULL may choose a default on some platforms).
snaplen should be non-negative; promisc non-zero to enable promiscuous mode; to_ms >= 0.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and use errbuf.

functions.name: pcap_open_dead
functions.description: Creates a dead (non-capturing) pcap handle for compiling filters or writing savefiles with a specified link-layer type and snapshot length.
requirements: linktype should be a LINKTYPE_* value; snaplen non-negative.
Handle is not usable for live capture; use for compile/write operations only.

functions.name: pcap_open_dead_with_tstamp_precision
functions.signature: pcap_t *pcap_open_dead_with_tstamp_precision(int linktype, int snaplen, u_int precision)
functions.description: Like pcap_open_dead(), but specifies timestamp precision (microsecond or nanosecond) for offline operations.
requirements: linktype should be LINKTYPE_*; snaplen non-negative.
precision must be PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_MICRO or PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_NANO.

functions.name: pcap_open_offline_with_tstamp_precision
functions.description: Opens a capture file for reading with requested timestamp precision interpretation.
requirements: fname must name a readable capture file.
precision must be PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_MICRO or PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_NANO.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and use errbuf.

functions.name: pcap_open_offline
functions.description: Opens a capture file for reading.
requirements: fname must name a readable capture file.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and use errbuf.

functions.name: pcap_fopen_offline_with_tstamp_precision
functions.description: Opens a capture file for reading from an existing FILE* with a requested timestamp precision interpretation (non-Windows API as declared; Windows provides HANDLE-based variants/macros).
requirements: fp must be a valid readable FILE* positioned at the start of a capture file.
precision must be PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_MICRO or PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_NANO.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and use errbuf.
On Windows, use pcap_hopen_offline_with_tstamp_precision via provided macros when not building libpcap.

functions.name: pcap_fopen_offline
functions.description: Opens a capture file for reading from an existing FILE* (non-Windows API as declared; Windows provides HANDLE-based variants/macros).
requirements: fp must be a valid readable FILE* at the appropriate position.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and use errbuf.
On Windows, use pcap_hopen_offline via the provided macro when not building libpcap.

functions.name: pcap_close
functions.description: Closes a pcap handle and releases associated resources.
requirements: p must be a pcap handle returned by an open/create routine; OK to pass NULL on some implementations but not guaranteed by header.
Do not use p after calling.

functions.name: pcap_loop
functions.signature: int pcap_loop(pcap_t *p, int cnt, pcap_handler callback, u_char *user)
functions.description: Processes packets from a live capture or offline file, invoking callback for each packet. Stops after cnt packets (if cnt > 0), on error, or when pcap_breakloop() is called.
requirements: p must be a valid active or offline handle.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with user, pcap_pkthdr*, and packet data.
cnt < 0 means loop forever; cnt == 0 means process all available in one buffer (platform-dependent) or none; cnt > 0 means process that many packets.
Caller must check return value (PCAP_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).

functions.name: pcap_dispatch
functions.signature: int pcap_dispatch(pcap_t *p, int cnt, pcap_handler callback, u_char *user)
functions.description: Processes up to cnt packets currently buffered/available, calling callback for each. Returns number of packets processed, 0 on timeout (live), or PCAP_ERROR_* on error.
requirements: p must be a valid active or offline handle.
callback must be a valid function pointer; user is opaque pointer passed through.
cnt semantics similar to pcap_loop; <= 0 may be treated specially by implementation.
Caller must check return value (PCAP_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).

functions.name: pcap_next
functions.description: Retrieves the next packet from a capture, filling the header and returning a pointer to the packet data, or NULL on error/timeout/end of file.
requirements: p must be a valid active or offline handle.
h must be a non-null pointer to a pcap_pkthdr to receive metadata.
Return pointer is valid until the next read call on p or handle close; copy data if needed.

functions.name: pcap_next_ex
functions.signature: int pcap_next_ex(pcap_t *p, struct pcap_pkthdr **pkt_header, const u_char **pkt_data)
functions.description: Retrieves the next packet with explicit status: 1 on success, 0 on timeout (live captures), -1 on error, -2 on EOF.
requirements: p must be a valid active or offline handle.
pkt_header and pkt_data must be non-null pointers to receive pointers.
Returned pkt_data pointer remains valid until next read on p or close; copy if needed.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: pcap_breakloop
functions.description: Causes an active pcap_loop() or pcap_dispatch() on the handle to return promptly with PCAP_ERROR_BREAK.
requirements: p must be a valid handle currently in a loop/dispatch; safe to call from another thread depending on platform.
After break, loops return PCAP_ERROR_BREAK.

functions.name: pcap_stats
functions.description: Retrieves capture statistics counters for the given live capture handle.
requirements: p must be an active live capture handle (not offline).
ps must be a valid non-null pointer to receive statistics.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_* on failure; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_setfilter
functions.description: Installs a compiled BPF filter on a capture handle to limit captured/returned traffic.
requirements: p must be an active capture handle (or some platforms allow pre-activation).
fp must point to a valid program compiled with pcap_compile().
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_setdirection
functions.description: Restricts packet direction (incoming/outgoing) for packets delivered to the application, if supported.
requirements: p must be a valid capture handle (typically active).
d must be one of PCAP_D_INOUT, PCAP_D_IN, or PCAP_D_OUT.
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_getnonblock
functions.description: Gets the non-blocking mode setting of a live capture handle, returning 0 or 1, or -1 on error with errbuf set.
requirements: p must be an active live capture handle.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: pcap_setnonblock
functions.description: Sets or clears non-blocking mode on a live capture handle.
requirements: p must be an active live capture handle.
nonblock non-zero enables non-blocking; zero disables.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_inject
functions.signature: int pcap_inject(pcap_t *p, const void *buf, size_t size)
functions.description: Transmits a raw packet through a capture handle, returning the number of bytes written or a PCAP_ERROR_* code.
requirements: p must be an active handle opened for injection on an interface that supports sending.
buf must point to a buffer of at least size bytes; size > 0.
Caller must check return (PCAP_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).

functions.name: pcap_sendpacket
functions.signature: int pcap_sendpacket(pcap_t *p, const u_char *buf, int size)
functions.description: Transmits a single raw packet buffer; returns 0 on success, PCAP_ERROR_* on failure.
requirements: p must be an active handle on a device that supports sending.
buf must point to a buffer of at least size bytes; size > 0.
Caller must check return (PCAP_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).

functions.name: pcap_statustostr
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing a libpcap status/error code (PCAP_ERROR_* or PCAP_WARNING_*).
requirements: error should be a PCAP_ERROR_* or PCAP_WARNING_* value; other integers may be mapped generically.
Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not free.

functions.name: pcap_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for a system or libpcap error code, similar to strerror().
requirements: error is an integer error code; mapping may be platform-specific.
Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not free.

functions.name: pcap_geterr
functions.description: Returns the last error message associated with the given pcap handle, as a string pointer.
requirements: p must be a valid pcap handle.
Returned pointer refers to internal storage that may change on subsequent errors; copy if needed.

functions.name: pcap_perror
functions.description: Prints the last error message for the handle to standard error, optionally prefixed.
requirements: p must be a valid pcap handle.
prefix may be NULL or a C string.

functions.name: pcap_compile
functions.signature: int pcap_compile(pcap_t *p, struct bpf_program *program, const char *buf, int optimize, bpf_u_int32 netmask)
functions.description: Compiles a filter expression into a BPF program for the link-layer type of the handle.
requirements: p must be a valid handle (dead, active, or offline) with known linktype/snaplen.
program must be a valid non-null pointer to receive compiled code; free with pcap_freecode().
buf must be a valid null-terminated filter expression string.
optimize is non-zero to enable optimizer; zero to disable.
netmask should be the IPv4 netmask for filter optimization (use PCAP_NETMASK_UNKNOWN if unknown).
Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_compile_nopcap
functions.signature: int pcap_compile_nopcap(int snaplen, int linktype, struct bpf_program *program, const char *buf, int optimize, bpf_u_int32 netmask)
functions.description: Compiles a filter expression without opening a capture handle, using the provided linktype and snaplen. Deprecated; prefer pcap_open_dead()+pcap_compile().
requirements: snaplen non-negative; linktype is a LINKTYPE_* value.
program must be a non-null pointer to receive compiled code; free with pcap_freecode().
buf must be a valid filter string; optimize and netmask as in pcap_compile().
Caller must check return (PCAP_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).

functions.name: pcap_freecode
functions.description: Frees the memory allocated for a compiled BPF program created by pcap_compile() or pcap_compile_nopcap().
requirements: program must point to a bpf_program previously filled by pcap_compile*().
Do not use program->bf_insns after freeing.

functions.name: pcap_offline_filter
functions.signature: int pcap_offline_filter(const struct bpf_program *program, const struct pcap_pkthdr *h, const u_char *pkt)
functions.description: Tests whether a packet would pass the given compiled filter program. Returns non-zero if accepted, zero if rejected.
requirements: program must be a valid compiled BPF program.
h must point to a valid packet header; pkt must point to at least h->caplen bytes of data.

functions.name: pcap_datalink
functions.description: Returns the link-layer header type (DLT_/LINKTYPE_ value) for the capture handle.
requirements: p must be a valid handle.
Caller must interpret return as an integer value; check for negative errors per implementation.

functions.name: pcap_datalink_ext
functions.description: Returns the extended link-layer type field from the file or handle (may include FCS length flags).
requirements: p must be a valid handle.
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: pcap_list_datalinks
functions.description: Retrieves a list of supported DLT_/LINKTYPE_ values that the handle can select via pcap_set_datalink().
requirements: p must be a valid handle.
dlt_buf must be a non-null pointer to receive allocated array; free with pcap_free_datalinks().
Returns count >= 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_* on failure; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_datalink
functions.description: Sets the link-layer header type (DLT_/LINKTYPE_) for the handle, if supported.
requirements: p must be a valid handle; typically set before activation or as supported by platform.
dlt must be a value from the list returned by pcap_list_datalinks().
Returns 0 on success or PCAP_ERROR_*; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_free_datalinks
functions.description: Frees an array of DLT values returned by pcap_list_datalinks().
requirements: dlt_list must be a pointer previously returned by pcap_list_datalinks(), or NULL.
Do not use after freeing.

functions.name: pcap_datalink_name_to_val
functions.description: Converts a DLT/linktype name string to its numeric value, or returns -1 if unknown.
requirements: name must be a valid null-terminated string.
Caller must check for -1 return.

functions.name: pcap_datalink_val_to_name
functions.description: Returns the canonical name for a DLT/linktype value, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: dlt should be a valid DLT_/LINKTYPE_ value.
Caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: pcap_datalink_val_to_description
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description for a DLT/linktype value, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: dlt should be a valid DLT_/LINKTYPE_ value.
Caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: pcap_datalink_val_to_description_or_dlt
functions.description: Returns a description for a DLT/linktype value, or a fallback string naming the numeric DLT if no description is known.
requirements: dlt is an integer linktype value.
Caller must check returned pointer (never specified as NULL in header; treat as const static string).

functions.name: pcap_snapshot
functions.description: Returns the snapshot length (maximum captured bytes per packet) for the capture handle.
requirements: p must be a valid handle.
Return is non-negative; caller should treat negative as error if applicable.

functions.name: pcap_is_swapped
functions.description: Indicates whether the savefile being read has byte order opposite to the host (offline captures).
requirements: p must be a valid handle; meaningful for offline file handles.
Returns 0 or 1.

functions.name: pcap_major_version
functions.description: Returns the major version number of the pcap savefile format for an offline capture handle.
requirements: p must be a valid offline handle; unspecified for live handles.

functions.name: pcap_minor_version
functions.description: Returns the minor version number of the pcap savefile format for an offline capture handle.
requirements: p must be a valid offline handle; unspecified for live handles.

functions.name: pcap_bufsize
functions.description: Returns the capture buffer size for a handle, if available.
requirements: p must be a valid handle.
Caller must handle negative/error returns per platform.

functions.name: pcap_file
functions.description: Returns the underlying FILE* for an offline capture, if any.
requirements: p must be a valid offline handle opened from a file.
Returned FILE* may be NULL on non-file sources; use only for offline files.

functions.name: pcap_fileno
functions.description: Returns a file descriptor (Unix) or similar integer for the capture handle. On Windows this is deprecated and may not be meaningful.
requirements: p must be a valid handle.
On Windows, function is deprecated and may not correspond to a usable HANDLE; prefer platform-specific APIs.
Caller must be prepared for negative error returns per platform.

functions.name: pcap_dump_open
functions.description: Opens a savefile for writing captured packets using the linktype/snaplen of handle p.
requirements: p must be a valid handle (live or dead) supplying linktype/snaplen.
fname must be a valid path; use "-" to write to standard output on some platforms.
Returns NULL on failure; use pcap_geterr(p) for details.

functions.name: pcap_dump_fopen
functions.description: Opens a savefile for writing to an existing FILE* using the linktype/snaplen of handle p (non-Windows API as declared; Windows provides HANDLE-based variant via macro when not building libpcap).
requirements: p must be a valid handle (live or dead) with linktype/snaplen.
fp must be a writable FILE* opened in binary mode.
Returns NULL on error; use pcap_geterr(p) for details.

functions.name: pcap_dump_open_append
functions.description: Opens a savefile for appending packets using the linktype/snaplen of handle p, creating it if necessary.
requirements: p must be a valid handle with linktype/snaplen.
fname must be a valid pathname.
Returns NULL on error; use pcap_geterr(p) for details.

functions.name: pcap_dump_file
functions.description: Returns the underlying FILE* associated with a dumper handle.
requirements: p must be a valid pcap_dumper_t*.
May return NULL in some environments; check before use.

functions.name: pcap_dump_ftell
functions.description: Returns the current file position for the dumper stream as a long, or -1 on error.
requirements: p must be a valid dumper handle.
Caller must check for -1 on error.

functions.name: pcap_dump_ftell64
functions.description: Returns the current file position for the dumper stream as a 64-bit integer, or -1 on error.
requirements: p must be a valid dumper handle.
Caller must check for negative on error.

functions.name: pcap_dump_flush
functions.description: Flushes buffered data to the dumper file. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: p must be a valid dumper handle.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: pcap_dump_close
functions.description: Closes the dumper and releases resources; also flushes buffered data.
requirements: p must be a valid dumper handle; after closing, p is invalid.
Safe to call when no further writes are pending.

functions.name: pcap_dump
functions.signature: void pcap_dump(u_char *user, const struct pcap_pkthdr *h, const u_char *sp)
functions.description: Writes a packet to the savefile associated with a dumper; typically used as a callback for pcap_loop/dispatch with user pointing to a pcap_dumper_t.
requirements: user must be a pcap_dumper_t* cast to u_char* as provided to pcap_loop/dispatch.
h must describe the packet; sp must point to at least h->caplen bytes.
The dumper must have been opened with pcap_dump_open/fopen.

functions.name: pcap_findalldevs
functions.description: Builds a linked list of all capture devices on the local host.
requirements: alldevs must be a non-null pointer to receive the head of a list; free with pcap_freealldevs().
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_freealldevs
functions.description: Frees a device list allocated by pcap_findalldevs() or pcap_findalldevs_ex().
requirements: alldevs must be a list pointer previously returned by a findalldevs function, or NULL.
Do not use the list after freeing.

functions.name: pcap_lib_version
functions.description: Returns a string describing the libpcap version and underlying components.
requirements: Returned pointer is to static storage; do not free.

functions.name: pcap_get_selectable_fd
functions.description: Unix-only: returns a file descriptor suitable for select()/poll(), or -1 if none is available for this handle.
requirements: Available only on non-Windows builds.
p must be a valid handle.
Caller must check for -1 and handle accordingly.

functions.name: pcap_get_required_select_timeout
functions.description: Unix-only: returns a required select() timeout for the given handle, or NULL if no specific requirement exists.
requirements: Available only on non-Windows builds.
p must be a valid handle.
Returned pointer may be to static storage; treat as read-only and do not free.

functions.name: pcap_open
functions.signature: pcap_t *pcap_open(const char *source, int snaplen, int flags, int read_timeout, struct pcap_rmtauth *auth, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Opens a capture source by URL-like string. Supports local savefiles, local interfaces, and remote RPCAP sources; combines creation, configuration, and activation.
requirements: source must follow one of the documented formats (e.g., file://..., rpcap://..., device name).
snaplen non-negative; flags may include PCAP_OPENFLAG_*; read_timeout >= 0.
auth may be NULL for local or unauthenticated access; for remote, may point to struct pcap_rmtauth with valid fields.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and use errbuf.

functions.name: pcap_createsrcstr
functions.signature: int pcap_createsrcstr(char *source, int type, const char *host, const char *port, const char *name, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Builds a source string suitable for pcap_open() from its components.
requirements: source must be a writable buffer large enough for the result (recommend at least PCAP_BUF_SIZE).
type must be one of PCAP_SRC_FILE, PCAP_SRC_IFLOCAL, or PCAP_SRC_IFREMOTE.
host/port/name may be NULL based on type; semantics follow documented formats.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_parsesrcstr
functions.signature: int pcap_parsesrcstr(const char *source, int *type, char *host, char *port, char *name, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Parses a source string into its components for inspection or modification.
requirements: source must be a valid null-terminated source string.
type must be a non-null pointer to receive the type.
host/port/name buffers, if non-NULL, must be large enough to hold parsed fields (recommend PCAP_BUF_SIZE).
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_findalldevs_ex
functions.signature: int pcap_findalldevs_ex(const char *source, struct pcap_rmtauth *auth, pcap_if_t **alldevs, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Lists capture devices or files from a source: scan directories, list local adapters, or list remote adapters over RPCAP.
requirements: source must follow documented pcap_findalldevs_ex() formats (e.g., file://folder/, rpcap://...).
auth may be NULL; provide for remote authenticated queries as needed.
alldevs must be non-null; free with pcap_freealldevs().
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_setsampling
functions.description: Windows-only feature support: enables and returns access to sampling configuration for the capture handle (affects what packets are returned).
requirements: Available primarily on Windows; sampling affects post-filter packets.
p must be a valid handle. Returns pointer to internal sampling struct or NULL if unsupported; do not free directly.

functions.name: pcap_remoteact_accept
functions.signature: PCAP_SOCKET pcap_remoteact_accept(const char *address, const char *port, const char *hostlist, char *connectinghost, struct pcap_rmtauth *auth, char *errbuf)
functions.description: RPCAP active mode: listens for and accepts an incoming active-mode connection from a remote probe, returning a connected socket.
requirements: address and port specify local bind parameters; hostlist defines allowed hosts (max RPCAP_HOSTLIST_SIZE).
connectinghost must be a writable buffer to receive the peer name; size not specified here (ensure sufficiently large).
auth may be NULL or point to credentials for remote authentication.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns an OS socket type (PCAP_SOCKET) or an invalid value on error; caller must check and use errbuf.

functions.name: pcap_remoteact_accept_ex
functions.signature: PCAP_SOCKET pcap_remoteact_accept_ex(const char *address, const char *port, const char *hostlist, char *connectinghost, struct pcap_rmtauth *auth, int uses_ssl, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Like pcap_remoteact_accept(), but allows specifying whether SSL/TLS is used for the active mode connection.
requirements: uses_ssl non-zero requests TLS if compiled with SSL support.
Other requirements as for pcap_remoteact_accept().
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.

functions.name: pcap_remoteact_list
functions.signature: int pcap_remoteact_list(char *hostlist, char sep, int size, char *errbuf)
functions.description: Retrieves a list of currently active-mode connected hosts into hostlist, separated by sep.
requirements: hostlist must be a writable buffer of length size (in bytes).
sep is the character used to separate host entries.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns >=0 on success (e.g., bytes written or count) or -1 on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_remoteact_close
functions.description: Closes an active-mode connection to the specified host.
requirements: host must identify an existing active-mode peer.
errbuf must be non-null and at least PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE bytes.
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_remoteact_cleanup
functions.description: Cleans up RPCAP active-mode internal state and closes any lingering resources.
requirements: Call when no active-mode sessions are needed.
Safe to call even if no sessions exist.

functions.name: pcap_alloc_option
functions.description: Allocates an options object for extended libpcap I/O configuration (e.g., plugins, timestamp precision).
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check and free with pcap_free_option().

functions.name: pcap_free_option
functions.description: Frees an options object allocated by pcap_alloc_option().
requirements: po must be a pointer previously returned by pcap_alloc_option(), or NULL.
Do not use po after freeing.

functions.name: pcap_set_option_string
functions.signature: int pcap_set_option_string(pcap_options *po, enum pcap_option_name pon, const char *value)
functions.description: Sets a string-valued option (e.g., plugin path) on an options object.
requirements: po must be a valid options object.
pon must be a string option constant (e.g., PON_IO_READ_PLUGIN or PON_IO_WRITE_PLUGIN).
value must be a valid null-terminated string.
Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_set_option_int
functions.signature: int pcap_set_option_int(pcap_options *po, enum pcap_option_name pon, const int value)
functions.description: Sets an integer-valued option (e.g., timestamp precision) on an options object.
requirements: po must be a valid options object.
pon must be an int option constant (e.g., PON_TSTAMP_PRECISION).
value must be within allowed range for the given option (e.g., PCAP_TSTAMP_PRECISION_* for precision).
Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error; caller must check return.

functions.name: pcap_get_option_string
functions.description: Gets the string value of an option from an options object, or NULL if unset/invalid.
requirements: po must be a valid options object.
pon must be a string option id.
Returned pointer may refer to internal storage; do not free; copy if needed.

functions.name: pcap_get_option_int
functions.description: Gets the integer value of an option from an options object.
requirements: po must be a valid options object.
pon must be an int option id.
Return value semantics are option-specific; caller must distinguish unset/invalid based on documented defaults (unknown here).

unharnessable_functions.name: pcap_set_protocol_linux
unharnessable_functions.reason: This API is only available on Linux builds and may be missing or behave differently on non-Linux toolchains, so we cannot reliably compile and link it in this fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: pcap_remoteact_accept

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target datatype: raw packet bytes
# Goal: produce valid, interesting packet-like byte buffers that exercise
# libpcap/BPF usage in the stubs:
# - bpf_filter: arbitrary bytes, lengths vary; interpreter inspects headers/offsets
# - pcap_inject / pcap_sendpacket: small L2 frames <= ~1500 bytes
# - pcap_offline_filter / pcap_dump: caplen truncated to <= 512 in stub
# Strategy:
# Generate a mix of realistic L2/L3/L4 payloads (Ethernet with IPv4/IPv6, ARP,
# VLAN tags, LLC/SNAP), and some non-Ethernet small blobs. Keep size <= 1500
# and typically <= 512 for offline/dump. Ensure variety via seed.
# We avoid malformed checksums on purpose because libpcap/BPF doesn't require
# valid checksums to parse header fields; but we compute simple checksums where
# cheap to do so for plausibility.

ETH_P_IP = 0x0800
ETH_P_ARP = 0x0806
ETH_P_IPV6 = 0x86DD
ETH_P_8021Q = 0x8100
ETH_P_LLDP = 0x88CC

IPPROTO_TCP = 6
IPPROTO_UDP = 17
IPPROTO_ICMP = 1
IPPROTO_ICMPV6 = 58

MAX_OUT = 1500


def mac_bytes(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Unicast locally administered MAC by default; sometimes broadcast/multicast
    kind = rnd.randrange(0, 10)
    if kind == 0:
        return b"\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff"  # broadcast
    if kind == 1:
        # IPv6 multicast 33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx
        return b"\x33\x33" + rnd.randbytes(4)
    # Locally administered, unicast: set LAA bit, clear multicast bit
    b0 = (rnd.randrange(0, 256) | 0x02) & 0xFE
    return bytes([b0]) + rnd.randbytes(5)


def checksum16(data: bytes) -> int:
    # Internet checksum
    s = 0
    n = len(data)
    i = 0
    while i + 1 < n:
        s += (data[i] << 8) + data[i + 1]
        s = (s & 0xFFFF) + (s >> 16)
        i += 2
    if n & 1:
        s += data[-1] << 8
        s = (s & 0xFFFF) + (s >> 16)
    return (~s) & 0xFFFF


def ipv4_hdr(rnd: random.Random, proto: int, total_len: int, src: bytes = None, dst: bytes = None) -> bytes:
    ver_ihl = 0x45  # no options
    tos = rnd.randrange(0, 256)
    identification = rnd.randrange(0, 65536)
    flags_frag = rnd.choice([0, 0x4000, 0x2000])  # DF, MF, or none (rarely MF without frag offset)
    frag_off = rnd.randrange(0, 8) if (flags_frag & 0x2000) else 0
    flags_frag |= frag_off
    ttl = rnd.randrange(32, 255)
    src_ip = src if src else rnd.randbytes(4)
    dst_ip = dst if dst else rnd.randbytes(4)
    header = struct.pack(
        '!BBHHHBBH4s4s',
        ver_ihl,
        tos,
        total_len,
        identification,
        flags_frag,
        ttl,
        proto,
        0,  # checksum placeholder
        src_ip,
        dst_ip,
    )
    csum = checksum16(header)
    header = header[:10] + struct.pack('!H', csum) + header[12:]
    return header


def udp_hdr(rnd: random.Random, src_port: int, dst_port: int, length: int, pseudo_sum: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # length includes UDP header (8) + payload
    hdr = struct.pack('!HHHH', src_port, dst_port, length, 0)
    # We leave checksum 0 sometimes (allowed for IPv4). For IPv6 it must be non-zero; we can compute pseudo if provided.
    if pseudo_sum:
        # compute checksum over pseudo header + UDP header + payload external later; here just return header with 0, caller will fix.
        return hdr
    else:
        return hdr


def tcp_hdr(rnd: random.Random, src_port: int, dst_port: int, seq: int, ack: int, flags: int, win: int, urg_ptr: int, data_offset_words: int = 5) -> bytes:
    off_res_flags = (data_offset_words << 12) | flags
    hdr = struct.pack('!HHIIHHHH', src_port, dst_port, seq, ack, off_res_flags, win, 0, urg_ptr)
    return hdr


def vlan_tag(vlan_id: int, pcp: int, dei: int) -> bytes:
    tci = ((pcp & 0x7) << 13) | ((dei & 0x1) << 12) | (vlan_id & 0x0FFF)
    return struct.pack('!HH', ETH_P_8021Q, tci)


def build_eth_frame(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    dst = mac_bytes(rnd)
    src = mac_bytes(rnd)

    # Choose encapsulation
    choice = rnd.randrange(0, 8)
    payload = b''
    ethertype = ETH_P_IP

    if choice == 0:
        # ARP request/reply (28 bytes typical IPv4 over Ethernet)
        ethertype = ETH_P_ARP
        htype = 1
        ptype = 0x0800
        hlen = 6
        plen = 4
        oper = rnd.choice([1, 2])
        sha = src
        spa = rnd.randbytes(4)
        tha = dst
        tpa = rnd.randbytes(4)
        payload = struct.pack('!HHBBH6s4s6s4s', htype, ptype, hlen, plen, oper, sha, spa, tha, tpa)
    elif choice == 1:
        # IPv4 + UDP with small payload
        udp_payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 64))
        udp_len = 8 + len(udp_payload)
        total_len = 20 + udp_len
        ip = ipv4_hdr(rnd, IPPROTO_UDP, total_len)
        uh = udp_hdr(rnd, rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), rnd.randrange(1, 65535), udp_len)
        payload = ip + uh + udp_payload
        ethertype = ETH_P_IP
    elif choice == 2:
        # IPv4 + TCP minimal header with flags (SYN/ACK/random)
        tcp_payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 32))
        tcph = tcp_hdr(
            rnd,
            rnd.randrange(1024, 65535),
            rnd.randrange(1, 65535),
            rnd.randrange(0, 2**32),
            rnd.randrange(0, 2**32),
            rnd.choice([0x02, 0x10, 0x12, 0x18]),  # SYN, ACK, SYN-ACK, PSH-ACK
            rnd.randrange(1024, 65535),
            0,
            5,
        )
        total_len = 20 + len(tcph) + len(tcp_payload)
        ip = ipv4_hdr(rnd, IPPROTO_TCP, total_len)
        payload = ip + tcph + tcp_payload
        ethertype = ETH_P_IP
    elif choice == 3:
        # IPv6 + UDP small payload
        udp_payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 64))
        payload_len = 8 + len(udp_payload)
        v_tc_fl = (6 << 28) | (rnd.randrange(0, 1 << 20))
        next_header = IPPROTO_UDP
        hop_limit = rnd.randrange(32, 255)
        src6 = rnd.randbytes(16)
        dst6 = rnd.randbytes(16)
        v6hdr = struct.pack('!IHBB16s16s', v_tc_fl, payload_len, next_header, hop_limit, src6, dst6)
        uh = udp_hdr(rnd, rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), rnd.randrange(1, 65535), 8 + len(udp_payload), pseudo_sum=1)
        # Compute UDP checksum for IPv6 (required)
        pseudo = src6 + dst6 + struct.pack('!I3xB', 8 + len(udp_payload), IPPROTO_UDP)
        csum = checksum16(pseudo + uh + udp_payload)
        uh = uh[:6] + struct.pack('!H', csum)
        payload = v6hdr + uh + udp_payload
        ethertype = ETH_P_IPV6
    elif choice == 4:
        # VLAN tagged IPv4 UDP
        inner_udp = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 32))
        udp_len = 8 + len(inner_udp)
        total_len = 20 + udp_len
        ip = ipv4_hdr(rnd, IPPROTO_UDP, total_len)
        uh = udp_hdr(rnd, rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), rnd.randrange(1, 65535), udp_len)
        inner = ip + uh + inner_udp
        vlan = vlan_tag(rnd.randrange(1, 4095), rnd.randrange(0, 8), rnd.randrange(0, 2))
        payload = vlan + struct.pack('!H', ETH_P_IP) + inner
        ethertype = ETH_P_8021Q
    elif choice == 5:
        # LLC/SNAP carrying IPv4
        snap_hdr = b"\xaa\xaa\x03\x00\x00\x00" + struct.pack('!H', ETH_P_IP)
        udp_payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 32))
        udp_len = 8 + len(udp_payload)
        total_len = 20 + udp_len
        ip = ipv4_hdr(rnd, IPPROTO_UDP, total_len)
        uh = udp_hdr(rnd, rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), rnd.randrange(1, 65535), udp_len)
        payload = snap_hdr + ip + uh + udp_payload
        # For 802.3/LLC frames, Ethernet length field should be payload length (<=1500). We still set ethertype like length.
        ethertype = len(payload) if len(payload) <= 1500 else 1500
    elif choice == 6:
        # LLDP minimal (not fully spec-compliant, but plausible TLVs)
        ethertype = ETH_P_LLDP
        # Chassis ID TLV (type=1)
        chassis = b"\x02" + rnd.randbytes(5)  # subtype 2 MAC + 5 bytes
        tlv1 = struct.pack('!H', (1 << 9) | len(chassis)) + chassis
        # Port ID TLV (type=2)
        port = b"\x05" + rnd.randbytes(3)
        tlv2 = struct.pack('!H', (2 << 9) | len(port)) + port
        # TTL TLV (type=3)
        ttlv = struct.pack('!H', 120)
        tlv3 = struct.pack('!H', (3 << 9) | len(ttlv)) + ttlv
        # End TLV (type=0, len=0)
        end = b"\x00\x00"
        payload = tlv1 + tlv2 + tlv3 + end
    else:
        # Raw payload bytes under IPv4 ethertype to let BPF parse L3 if needed
        ethertype = ETH_P_IP
        payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 128))

    # Build Ethernet header
    eth_hdr = dst + src + struct.pack('!H', ethertype if isinstance(ethertype, int) else ethertype)
    frame = eth_hdr + payload

    # Ensure minimum Ethernet payload of 46 bytes (pad) for classic Ethernet (not strictly required for our userspace buffers, but fine)
    if len(frame) < 60:
        frame += b"\x00" * (60 - len(frame))

    # Cap to MTU-like size to satisfy stubs
    if len(frame) > MAX_OUT:
        frame = frame[:MAX_OUT]
    return frame


def build_ip_packet_only(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce standalone IP packet bytes (no Ethernet) for diversity
    choice = rnd.randrange(0, 3)
    if choice == 0:
        # IPv4 UDP
        udp_payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 200))
        udp_len = 8 + len(udp_payload)
        total_len = 20 + udp_len
        ip = ipv4_hdr(rnd, IPPROTO_UDP, total_len)
        uh = udp_hdr(rnd, rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), rnd.randrange(1, 65535), udp_len)
        return ip + uh + udp_payload
    elif choice == 1:
        # IPv4 TCP
        tcp_payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 200))
        tcph = tcp_hdr(
            rnd,
            rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), rnd.randrange(1, 65535),
            rnd.randrange(0, 2**32), rnd.randrange(0, 2**32),
            rnd.choice([0x02, 0x10, 0x11, 0x18]),
            rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), 0, 5
        )
        total_len = 20 + len(tcph) + len(tcp_payload)
        ip = ipv4_hdr(rnd, IPPROTO_TCP, total_len)
        return ip + tcph + tcp_payload
    else:
        # IPv6 UDP minimal
        udp_payload = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 200))
        payload_len = 8 + len(udp_payload)
        v_tc_fl = (6 << 28) | (rnd.randrange(0, 1 << 20))
        next_header = IPPROTO_UDP
        hop_limit = rnd.randrange(32, 255)
        src6 = rnd.randbytes(16)
        dst6 = rnd.randbytes(16)
        v6hdr = struct.pack('!IHBB16s16s', v_tc_fl, payload_len, next_header, hop_limit, src6, dst6)
        uh = udp_hdr(rnd, rnd.randrange(1024, 65535), rnd.randrange(1, 65535), 8 + len(udp_payload), pseudo_sum=1)
        pseudo = src6 + dst6 + struct.pack('!I3xB', 8 + len(udp_payload), IPPROTO_UDP)
        csum = checksum16(pseudo + uh + udp_payload)
        uh = uh[:6] + struct.pack('!H', csum)
        return v6hdr + uh + udp_payload


def build_misc_blob(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Random non-protocol blob: useful to see BPF bounds checks
    n = rnd.randrange(1, 256)
    return rnd.randbytes(n)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a profile: Ethernet frame, IP-only, or misc blob.
    profile = rnd.choices(
        population=["eth", "ip", "blob"],
        weights=[60, 25, 15],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if profile == "eth":
        pkt = build_eth_frame(rnd)
    elif profile == "ip":
        pkt = build_ip_packet_only(rnd)
    else:
        pkt = build_misc_blob(rnd)

    # Keep size within 4096 per requirement, and also vary truncation to exercise buflen vs wirelen in bpf_filter stub.
    # We may sometimes append benign padding to simulate wirelen > buflen scenarios in the fuzzer's selection.
    if len(pkt) > 4096:
        pkt = pkt[:4096]

    # Occasionally create a slightly larger buffer up to 1024 to give room for fuzzer to choose buflen smaller than size
    if len(pkt) < 256 and rnd.random() < 0.5:
        pad = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randrange(0, 256 - len(pkt)))
        pkt = pkt + pad

    return bytes(pkt)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single bytes buffer intended to be used where
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR provides a hostname/FQDN string. We focus on generating
# valid, interesting host-like strings that exercise different resolver paths
# (ASCII labels, Unicode/punycode-like, numeric IPv4/IPv6 literals, localhost,
# SRV-like names, trailing dots, underscores, hyphen edge cases, long labels,
# and mixed-case). The output is a null-terminated or plain string buffer; the
# fuzzer stub uses std::string(c_str()), so a raw bytes sequence without NUL is
# fine. We avoid embedding NUL in the middle to keep it a single C string.

MAX_TOTAL_LEN = 512  # keep well under 4096 as requested

LDH = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
LABEL_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
UNICODE_LABELS = [
    "münchen",   # umlaut
    "пример",    # Cyrillic
    "例え",       # Japanese
    "δοκιμή",    # Greek
    "مثال",      # Arabic
]

GENERIC_TLDS = [
    "com", "org", "net", "edu", "gov", "io", "dev", "local", "test"
]

SECOND_LEVELS = [
    "www", "api", "mail", "ftp", "ns1", "ns2", "_sip", "_xmpp", "_ldap"
]

SPECIAL_HOSTS = [
    "localhost",
    "localhost.localdomain",
    "example.com",
    "example.org",
    "intranet",
]

IPV4_SAMPLES = [
    "127.0.0.1", "0.0.0.0", "255.255.255.255", "192.168.0.1", "10.0.0.1", "172.16.0.1"
]

IPV6_SAMPLES = [
    "::1", "::", "2001:db8::1", "fe80::1", "2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334",
    "[2001:db8::1]",  # bracketed form often used in URLs
]

def rand_label(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 20) -> str:
    # DNS label rules: 1-63 chars, alnum and hyphen, cannot start/end with hyphen
    L = rng.randint(min_len, min(max_len, 63))
    if L == 1:
        return rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    # Ensure start/end alnum
    middle_len = max(0, L - 2)
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    end = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    middle = "".join(rng.choice(LABEL_CHARS) for _ in range(middle_len))
    return start + middle + end

def hyphen_edge_label(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Valid label that includes hyphens but not at edges
    core = "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(3))
    return f"a-{core}-b"

def long_label(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Max length label (63 chars)
    L = 63
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    end = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    middle = "".join(rng.choice(LABEL_CHARS) for _ in range(L - 2))
    return start + middle[:-1] + end  # ensure length 63 and end alnum

def maybe_trailing_dot(rng: random.Random, host: str) -> str:
    return host + ("." if rng.random() < 0.3 and not host.endswith('.') else "")

def mixed_case(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    chars = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.5:
            chars.append(ch.upper())
        else:
            chars.append(ch)
    return "".join(chars)

def build_hostname_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    variants: List[str] = []

    # Basic FQDN
    labels = [rand_label(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))]
    labels[-1] = rng.choice(GENERIC_TLDS)
    variants.append(".".join(labels))

    # With underscore service labels (common in SRV records)
    variants.append(".".join([rng.choice(["_sip", "_xmpp", "_imap", "_ldap"]) , "_tcp", rand_label(rng), rng.choice(GENERIC_TLDS)]))

    # Long label plus normal suffix
    variants.append(".".join([long_label(rng), rand_label(rng, 2, 10), rng.choice(GENERIC_TLDS)]))

    # Hyphen edge case label
    variants.append(".".join([hyphen_edge_label(rng), rand_label(rng), rng.choice(GENERIC_TLDS)]))

    # Common names
    variants.extend(SPECIAL_HOSTS)

    # Numeric literals
    variants.extend(IPV4_SAMPLES)
    variants.extend(IPV6_SAMPLES)

    # Unicode labels (some resolvers may reject; still interesting but valid text)
    uni = rng.choice(UNICODE_LABELS)
    variants.append(f"{uni}.example")

    # Single-label host
    variants.append(rand_label(rng, 3, 12))

    # FQDN with many short labels
    many = ".".join(rand_label(rng, 1, 3) for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 10))) + "." + rng.choice(GENERIC_TLDS)
    variants.append(many)

    # Add trailing-dot variants and mixed-case versions
    out: List[str] = []
    for v in variants:
        v2 = maybe_trailing_dot(rng, v)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            v2 = mixed_case(rng, v2)
        out.append(v2)
    return out

def choose_interesting(rng: random.Random, candidates: List[str]) -> str:
    # Prefer to vary across categories by weighted choice
    weights = []
    for c in candidates:
        if c in IPV4_SAMPLES:
            w = 1.2
        elif c in IPV6_SAMPLES:
            w = 1.1
        elif c in SPECIAL_HOSTS:
            w = 1.0
        elif any(ch in c for ch in ["_", "-"]):
            w = 1.3
        elif any(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in c):
            w = 1.4
        elif c.endswith('.'):
            w = 1.2
        else:
            w = 1.0
        # penalize very long total strings beyond MAX_TOTAL_LEN
        if len(c) > MAX_TOTAL_LEN:
            w *= 0.2
        weights.append(w)
    total = sum(weights)
    r = rng.random() * total
    acc = 0.0
    for c, w in zip(candidates, weights):
        acc += w
        if r <= acc:
            return c[:MAX_TOTAL_LEN]
    return candidates[0][:MAX_TOTAL_LEN]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = build_hostname_variants(rng)
    choice = choose_interesting(rng, candidates)
    # Ensure it's non-empty and within size limit
    if not choice:
        choice = "localhost"
    choice = choice[:MAX_TOTAL_LEN]
    # Return UTF-8 bytes (libpcap APIs accept char*; typical environments are UTF-8 capable or treat bytes opaquely)
    return choice.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
